advanced-partial-f.name: Partial F major — four strings
advanced-partial-f.description: Strings 6 and 5 are silent. String 4: fret 3, ring finger. String 3: fret 2, middle finger. Strings 2 and 1: fret 1, one index finger spanning both. Low to high: F3, A3, C4, F4. The two finger-1 dots indicate one short barre, not two separate fingers.
advanced-partial-f.textAlternative: Strings 6 and 5 are silent. String 4: fret 3, ring finger. String 3: fret 2, middle finger. Strings 2 and 1: fret 1, one index finger spanning both. Low to high: F3, A3, C4, F4. The two finger-1 dots indicate one short barre, not two separate fingers.

advanced-g5-two-note.name: G5 — root and fifth
advanced-g5-two-note.description: Play strings 6 and 5 only: fret 3 with index, fret 5 with ring. Keep strings 4 through 1 silent. Low to high: G2, D3.
advanced-g5-two-note.textAlternative: Play strings 6 and 5 only: fret 3 with index, fret 5 with ring. Keep strings 4 through 1 silent. Low to high: G2, D3.

advanced-g5-three-note.name: G5 — root, fifth, octave
advanced-g5-three-note.description: Play strings 6, 5, 4: frets 3, 5, 5 with index, ring, little finger. Keep strings 3 through 1 silent. Low to high: G2, D3, G3.
advanced-g5-three-note.textAlternative: Play strings 6, 5, 4: frets 3, 5, 5 with index, ring, little finger. Keep strings 3 through 1 silent. Low to high: G2, D3, G3.

advanced-a5-three-note.name: A5 — root on string 6
advanced-a5-three-note.description: Play strings 6, 5, 4: frets 5, 7, 7 with index, ring, little finger. Keep strings 3 through 1 silent. Low to high: A2, E3, A3.
advanced-a5-three-note.textAlternative: Play strings 6, 5, 4: frets 5, 7, 7 with index, ring, little finger. Keep strings 3 through 1 silent. Low to high: A2, E3, A3.

advanced-c5-three-note.name: C5 — root on string 5
advanced-c5-three-note.description: Keep string 6 silent. Play strings 5, 4, 3: frets 3, 5, 5 with index, ring, little finger. Keep strings 2 and 1 silent. Low to high: C3, G3, C4.
advanced-c5-three-note.textAlternative: Keep string 6 silent. Play strings 5, 4, 3: frets 3, 5, 5 with index, ring, little finger. Keep strings 2 and 1 silent. Low to high: C3, G3, C4.

panels.label: Build a new entry
panels.action: Start with all fretting fingers off the strings. Set partial F: xx3211 from string 6 to string 1. No tempo requirement.

panels.label: Hear four strings
panels.action: Pick strings 4, 3, 2, 1 separately: F, A, C, F. Each must ring clearly. A dead or buzzing string makes this entry a repair attempt.

panels.label: Check the strum
panels.action: Down-strum only strings 4 through 1. Keep strings 6 and 5 quiet. Do not count four re-plucks of a held shape as four entries.

panels.label: Release and count
panels.action: Silence the chord with the picking hand, then take the fretting fingers off. Count one successful entry only after the four-string check, short strum, and release. Four consecutive entries is the goal; a failed entry resets the consecutive count.

advanced-switchyard-map.name: Switchyard — an original sixteen-bar power-chord piece
advanced-switchyard-map.provenance: Original GuitarHub instructional composition. Not an arrangement or transcription of a commercial song.

panels.label: Meter and shapes
panels.action: Switchyard is 16 bars of 4/4 in standard tuning, no capo. Use the three-string G5, A5 and C5 diagrams. Each chord name occupies one whole bar. G5 and A5 start on string 6; C5 starts on string 5.

panels.label: The repeating riff cell
panels.action: In EVERY bar: down-strum the named chord on beat 1; stop its sound on beat 2; down-strum again on beat 3; stop on beat 4. Count 1, 2, 3, 4 throughout. Rest through all of beats 2 and 4. This gives 32 attacks in the complete piece.

panels.label: A — bars 1 through 4
panels.action: Bar 1: G5. Bar 2: G5. Bar 3: A5. Bar 4: G5. Apply the same play, stop, play, stop cell in every bar.

panels.label: B — bars 5 through 8
panels.action: Bar 5: C5. Bar 6: C5. Bar 7: G5. Bar 8: G5. Use the silent beat 4 before a change to aim the next root; keep the strings muted while moving.

panels.label: A returns — bars 9 through 12
panels.action: Bar 9: G5. Bar 10: G5. Bar 11: A5. Bar 12: G5. Keep the second A section at the same pulse as the first.

panels.label: Ending — bars 13 through 16
panels.action: Bar 13: C5. Bar 14: A5. Bar 15: G5. Bar 16: G5. Play both attacks in bar 16, then stop on beat 4. There is no extra final strum.

panels.label: Count in and prepare
panels.action: Keep this map visible and use a separate metronome set to quarter-note clicks in 4/4. If using the iOS Practice metronome, copy the bar map before opening it. Begin with four silent count-in beats, then bar 1. Start practice at 60 BPM or slower if needed. The separate checkpoint target is 110 BPM.

panels.label: Review the take
panels.action: Count the silent beats as carefully as the attacks. Hear no pitched open string during the rests or chord moves. If you lose the bar, mute, keep counting, and re-enter at the next four-bar section during practice; label that take interrupted. A full checkpoint take has no restarts or skipped bars.

advanced-a7-open.name: A7 — open
advanced-a7-open.description: x02020 from strings 6 to 1. Index: string 4 fret 2. Middle: string 2 fret 2. Sound strings 5–1; low to high A2, E3, G3, C#4, E4. Exclude string 6.
advanced-a7-open.textAlternative: x02020 from strings 6 to 1. Index: string 4 fret 2. Middle: string 2 fret 2. Sound strings 5–1; low to high A2, E3, G3, C#4, E4. Exclude string 6.

advanced-d7-open.name: D7 — open
advanced-d7-open.description: xx0212 from strings 6 to 1. Middle: string 3 fret 2. Index: string 2 fret 1. Ring: string 1 fret 2. Sound strings 4–1: D3, A3, C4, F#4.
advanced-d7-open.textAlternative: xx0212 from strings 6 to 1. Middle: string 3 fret 2. Index: string 2 fret 1. Ring: string 1 fret 2. Sound strings 4–1: D3, A3, C4, F#4.

advanced-e7-open.name: E7 — open
advanced-e7-open.description: 020100 from strings 6 to 1. Middle: string 5 fret 2. Index: string 3 fret 1. Sound all six: E2, B2, D3, G#3, B3, E4.
advanced-e7-open.textAlternative: 020100 from strings 6 to 1. Middle: string 5 fret 2. Index: string 3 fret 1. Sound all six: E2, B2, D3, G#3, B3, E4.

panels.label: Choose this version
panels.action: Use this exact 12-bar form in A, in 4/4, with no quick change in bar 2. One chord per bar. Roman numerals I7, IV7 and V7 mean A7, D7 and E7 here.

panels.label: Bars 1–4
panels.action: Bar 1 A7; bar 2 A7; bar 3 A7; bar 4 A7. Say each bar number on its first beat, then count 2, 3, 4.

panels.label: Bars 5–8
panels.action: Bar 5 D7; bar 6 D7; bar 7 A7; bar 8 A7. Keep four beats in every bar, even when the same chord repeats.

panels.label: Bars 9–12
panels.action: Bar 9 E7; bar 10 D7; bar 11 A7; bar 12 E7. The E7 at bar 12 leads to A7 at bar 1 of the next chorus.

panels.label: Play a clear skeleton
panels.action: Choose a separate metronome around 60 BPM, or slower if needed. Give four count-in beats, then one gentle downstroke on beat 1 of each bar, allowing the chord to ring through 2, 3, 4. This is a straight counted skeleton, not a shuffle-rhythm test.

panels.label: Three-chorus check
panels.action: Repeat the exact form three times: 36 bars total, with no extra count-in or extra bar between choruses. After beat 4 of bar 12 in chorus 3, mute and finish. Hide or cover the map for the memory check; the lesson has no automatic chart-hide or bar-call control.

panels.label: How to call
panels.action: On beat 4 of the CURRENT bar, say the chord for the NEXT bar. Continue playing the current chord until the next beat 1. Say E-seven, not a bare number that could be confused with the bar count.

panels.label: First line
panels.action: During bars 1, 2 and 3, call A7 for the next bar. During bar 4, call D7 for bar 5.

panels.label: Middle line
panels.action: During bar 5, call D7; during bar 6, call A7; during bar 7, call A7; during bar 8, call E7.

panels.label: Last line
panels.action: During bar 9, call D7; during bar 10, call A7; during bar 11, call E7; during bar 12, call A7 for the next chorus.

panels.label: Fade the prompt
panels.action: First speak every next-bar chord with this guide. Next speak only before an actual chord change. Finally cover the guide and call from memory. These are your own spoken prompts, or a partner’s; no automatic app voice is provided.

advanced-a-blues-palette.title: A minor-pentatonic note choices on string 1
advanced-a-blues-palette.provenance: Original GuitarHub instructional note set; not a commercial-song transcription. Per-note synthesized references only.
advanced-a-blues-palette.instruction: This is a note map, not a timed scale run. Move the whole hand to reach a new position; do not stretch from fret 5 to 17. Start with A at 5 and C at 8; add E at 12 only when the move is comfortable. A, C, D, E, G is the A minor-pentatonic palette used over the A blues form. Its C is a deliberate blues colour against A7’s C#, not the A-major scale.

advanced-solo-seed.title: Original question: A, C, E
advanced-solo-seed.provenance: Original GuitarHub instructional note set; not a commercial-song transcription. Per-note synthesized references only.
advanced-solo-seed.instruction: One bar of 4/4: play A/fret 5 on beat 1 for one beat, C/fret 8 on beat 2 for one beat, and E/fret 12 on beat 3 for two beats. Stop at the next bar line. The buttons play individual pitches only; sing or play the written rhythm yourself.

advanced-solo-answers.name: Three possible answers to the original question

panels.label: Bar 1 — question
panels.action: At a comfortable quarter-note pulse, play string 1 fret 5 on beat 1, fret 8 on beat 2, and fret 12 on beat 3, holding through beat 4. These notes are A, C, E.

panels.label: Bar 2 — answer one
panels.action: Play C at fret 8 on beat 1 and hold for two beats. Play A at fret 5 on beat 3 and hold for two beats. The ending returns home.

panels.label: Bar 3 — answer two
panels.action: Play A at fret 5 on beat 1, C at fret 8 on beat 2, and A at fret 5 on beat 3, holding through beat 4. This keeps the question’s rhythm and changes its ending.

panels.label: Bar 4 — answer three
panels.action: Rest for beat 1. Play C at fret 8 on beat 2, E at fret 12 on beat 3, and A at fret 5 on beat 4. Each note lasts one beat; stop at the next bar line.

panels.label: Now make your own
panels.action: The written answers are demonstrations, not an improvisation pass. Invent three answers by changing a rhythm, ending, or rest while staying inside A, C, D, E, G. Keep counting through silence and finish each response within its allotted bar.

advanced-semitone-reference.title: Semitone reference: F#4 to G4 on string 2
advanced-semitone-reference.provenance: Original GuitarHub instructional note set; not a commercial-song transcription. Per-note synthesized references only.
advanced-semitone-reference.instruction: Fret 8 supplies the target pitch. For the bend, stay at fret 7 and bend string 2 toward the thicker strings until its pitch matches that G4. Do not slide to fret 8 during the bend. Buttons provide separate synthesized notes, not a bend recording or a live cents meter.

panels.label: Prepare the measurement
panels.action: Use your own chromatic tuner or pitch meter that shows G4 and cents at A4 = 440 Hz. Confirm the unbent reference at string 2 fret 8. GuitarHub’s standard-string tuner does not measure this G4 target.

panels.label: Define one attempt
panels.action: Pick F#4 at string 2 fret 7, bend to G4, and try to hold that pitch for one second without vibrato or a second pick. Mute before releasing. A success needs a stable G4 reading within −20 to +20 cents for that hold; a brief crossing is insufficient.

panels.label: Hide live feedback
panels.action: For the checkpoint, look away from the meter before picking. A helper can observe it, or you can review your own external tuner recording afterward. Do not steer the bend using the live display. No observer or usable recording means the numeric result remains unverified.

panels.label: Keep all four
panels.action: Number four attempts in advance and keep them in order, resting between each. Record the actual observed result for every attempt. No reading is unknown, not success; do not replace a failed bend with a later good one inside the same set.

panels.label: Report the result
panels.action: The target is at least three successful attempts in one fully observed set of four. Report ear-only practice separately when you lack numeric evidence. There is no in-app four-attempt grader or saved cents record for this exercise.

advanced-three-key-map.name: I, IV, V and vi in C, G and D major

panels.label: Build the quality pattern
panels.action: For these major keys: I, IV and V are major; vi is minor. In the spoken title, six means the sixth scale degree, not a major VI chord. Add m when naming the sixth chord.

panels.label: C major
panels.action: Scale: C D E F G A B. I = C (C E G); IV = F (F A C); V = G (G B D); vi = Am (A C E).

panels.label: G major
panels.action: Scale: G A B C D E F#. I = G (G B D); IV = C (C E G); V = D (D F# A); vi = Em (E G B).

panels.label: D major
panels.action: Scale: D E F# G A B C#. I = D (D F# A); IV = G (G B D); V = A (A C# E); vi = Bm (B D F#).

panels.label: Read the small voicings

panels.label: Positions
panels.action: String 6 roots: fret 1 F; fret 3 G; fret 5 A; fret 7 B; fret 8 C. Check E-shape major and minor at every position: ten separate shape-and-quality responses.

panels.label: One response
panels.action: Start released. Read or hear a fret and quality, name the chord, form it, pick strings 6 through 1 separately, strum, then mute and release. All six intended strings must ring; a repaired held grip is practice before a new fresh response.

panels.label: Mix the prompts
panels.action: Write the ten fret/quality pairs on slips and shuffle them yourself, or have a partner mix them. Every pair appears once. GuitarHub does not supply an automatic random caller.

panels.label: Keep the evidence
panels.action: Record which root, quality or string failed. A full self-check contains all ten fresh responses, with no substitution of easier positions or four-string shapes.

panels.label: Voicings and pulse
panels.action: Use G major as an E-shape barre at fret 3; C and D major as A-shape barres at frets 3 and 5. In 4/4, play downstrokes on beats 1 and 3, sustaining each for two beats. Use a separate metronome around 60 BPM; no automatic backing track is supplied.

panels.label: Bars 1–4
panels.action: Bar 1 G; bar 2 G; bar 3 C; bar 4 C. Every chord label occupies a whole four-beat bar.

panels.label: Bars 5–8
panels.action: Bar 5 G; bar 6 G; bar 7 D; bar 8 D.

panels.label: Bars 9–12
panels.action: Bar 9 C; bar 10 D; bar 11 G; bar 12 G.

panels.label: Bars 13–16
panels.action: Bar 13 C; bar 14 D; bar 15 G; bar 16 G. Make both attacks in the final bar and mute at the next bar line; no added ending chord.

panels.label: Full form
panels.action: Count in for four beats, then play all sixteen bars in order: 32 attacks. Use a small pressure release just before a change, keeping time and avoiding an open-string sweep. A restart or skipped bar makes the take interrupted.

l6-nearby-keys.name: Nearby I–IV–V roots in three major keys

panels.label: G major
panels.action: I = G, E-shape root on string 6 fret 3. IV = C, A-shape root on string 5 fret 3. V = D, A-shape root on string 5 fret 5. Return to G at fret 3.

panels.label: A major
panels.action: I = A, E-shape root on string 6 fret 5. IV = D, A-shape root on string 5 fret 5. V = E, A-shape root on string 5 fret 7. Return to A at fret 5.

panels.label: C major
panels.action: I = C, E-shape root on string 6 fret 8. IV = F, A-shape root on string 5 fret 8. V = G, A-shape root on string 5 fret 10. Return to C at fret 8.

panels.label: Practice form
panels.action: One four-beat bar each: I, IV, V, I. Begin with one downstroke on beat 1 and count the other three beats. The roots use a two-fret span within each key; this is a defined nearby route, not proof of the globally smallest movement.

l6-g-major-five-views.name: Five CAGED-region views of G major

panels.label: One note collection
panels.action: All five views contain G,A,B,C,D,E,F#. They follow the overlapping CAGED chord-form regions E,D,C,A,G up this part of the neck. They are maps, not five different keys, five full-scale performances, or a requirement to hold one finger across a whole window.

panels.label: E view
panels.action: E view, frets 2–5. String 6: 2(F#), 3(G), 5(A); String 5: 2(B), 3(C), 5(D); String 4: 2(E), 4(F#), 5(G); String 3: 2(A), 4(B), 5(C); String 2: 3(D), 5(E); String 1: 2(F#), 3(G), 5(A). Play one note at a time, never all listed frets as a chord.

panels.label: D view
panels.action: D view, frets 4–8. String 6: 5(A), 7(B), 8(C); String 5: 5(D), 7(E); String 4: 4(F#), 5(G), 7(A); String 3: 4(B), 5(C), 7(D); String 2: 5(E), 7(F#), 8(G); String 1: 5(A), 7(B), 8(C). Play one note at a time, never all listed frets as a chord.

panels.label: C view
panels.action: C view, frets 7–10. String 6: 7(B), 8(C), 10(D); String 5: 7(E), 9(F#), 10(G); String 4: 7(A), 9(B), 10(C); String 3: 7(D), 9(E); String 2: 7(F#), 8(G), 10(A); String 1: 7(B), 8(C), 10(D). Play one note at a time, never all listed frets as a chord.

panels.label: A view
panels.action: A view, frets 9–12. String 6: 10(D), 12(E); String 5: 9(F#), 10(G), 12(A); String 4: 9(B), 10(C), 12(D); String 3: 9(E), 11(F#), 12(G); String 2: 10(A), 12(B); String 1: 10(D), 12(E). Play one note at a time, never all listed frets as a chord.

panels.label: G view
panels.action: G view, frets 12–15. String 6: 12(E), 14(F#), 15(G); String 5: 12(A), 14(B), 15(C); String 4: 12(D), 14(E); String 3: 12(G), 14(A); String 2: 12(B), 13(C), 15(D); String 1: 12(E), 14(F#), 15(G). Play one note at a time, never all listed frets as a chord.

panels.label: Find roots and overlaps
panels.action: Locate G at string 6 fret 3, string 4 fret 5, string 2 fret 8, string 5 fret 10, string 3 fret 12 and string 1 fret 15. A note appearing in two neighbouring views is the same pitch location; use it to connect the maps.

l6-three-position-route.title: Three-position G-major connection
l6-three-position-route.provenance: Original GuitarHub instructional note sequence; isolated synthesized pitch references, not a commercial-song transcription or full audio performance.
l6-three-position-route.instruction: Four bars, one note per quarter-note beat. Follow the separate hand-position guide; the reference cells play individual notes only. Actual 100 BPM is the later checkpoint target, not the default speed of these buttons.

panels.label: First move
panels.action: Bar 1: frets 3,5,7,8. Play 3 with middle and 5 with little finger in the E view; then move the hand into the D view for ring on 7 and little on 8. One note on each beat.

panels.label: Second move
panels.action: Bar 2: frets 10,8,7,5. Move into the C view for little on 10, middle on 8, index on 7; return to the E view for little on 5. Shift pressure lightly between attacks without adding a beat.

panels.label: Repeat and finish
panels.action: Bar 3 repeats bar 1. Bar 4: frets 10,8,7,3, using the C-view fingering for 10,8,7, then the E-view middle finger on 3. Sustain that final G for its beat and mute at the next bar line.

panels.label: Check the whole route
panels.action: Four count-in beats precede the sixteen quarter-note attacks. In practice, isolate each shift slowly; in a full take, keep all four beats in each bar. The app does not detect the hand position or score this connection.

panels.label: The accompaniment
panels.action: Use a partner or your own separate recording for eight bars of 4/4: G,G,Em,Em,C,C,D,D. Each chord lasts two bars. No backing track or automatic arrival detector is supplied in this lesson.

panels.label: Chord-tone choices
panels.action: G contains G,B,D; Em contains E,G,B; C contains C,E,G; D contains D,F#,A. These all belong to G major. Choose one destination tone before each new chord.

panels.label: Thirds route
panels.action: For the specific third-target exercise, land B4 at bar 1, G4 at bar 3, E4 at bar 5 and F#4 at bar 7. On string 1 these are frets 7,3,0,2.

panels.label: Make the arrival audible
panels.action: Sound the destination on beat 1 of its arrival bar and hold it for at least that first beat. Use the remaining time for a short phrase or planned silence; do not stop counting.

panels.label: Eight-bar check
panels.action: One full take includes all eight bars and all four planned arrivals at bars 1,3,5,7. The checkpoint permits a root, third or fifth of each chord; state your choices before the take. Finish by the end of bar 8 without a restart.

l6-third-note-reference.title: Thirds of G, Em, C and D
l6-third-note-reference.provenance: Original GuitarHub instructional note sequence; isolated synthesized pitch references, not a commercial-song transcription or full audio performance.
l6-third-note-reference.instruction: These are four reference destinations, not a four-beat performance: B is G’s third, G is Em’s third, E is C’s third, F# is D’s third. In the eight-bar map they arrive at bars 1,3,5,7 respectively.

panels.label: Learner preparation
panels.action: Learner: look away before the helper reads the next panel. Use a guitar-playing helper and a separate click around 60 BPM. The learner hears the notes without seeing frets or note names; the app does not provide hidden-answer phrase audio.

panels.label: Helper answer key
panels.action: Helper only: play string 1 frets 3,5,7,3, one quarter note each, after four count-in beats. Pitches are G4,A4,B4,G4. Repeat the same four-note phrase on request; do not change the order or show your hand to the learner.

panels.label: Compare after the attempt
panels.action: Keep the learner’s first written four-note answer before revealing the key. Compare the sounded notes and their one-beat durations. If the learner saw the key beforehand, label the exercise familiar-phrase practice, not fresh transcription.

panels.label: Learner preparation
panels.action: Learner: do not read the helper answer panels before writing your first complete transcription. The helper should read them while you look away, then perform the exact original phrase at a comfortable, unchanged tempo. No blind audio playback is supplied by the app.

panels.label: Helper bar 1
panels.action: Helper only, bar 1: event 1: string 1 fret 3 (G4), onset 1, length 0.5 beats; event 2: string 1 fret 5 (A4), onset 1&, length 0.5 beats; event 3: string 1 fret 7 (B4), onset 2, length 1 beat; event 4: string 1 fret 10 (D5), onset 3, length 1 beat; event 5: string 1 fret 7 (B4), onset 4, length 1 beat.

panels.label: Helper bar 2
panels.action: Helper only, bar 2: event 6: string 1 fret 5 (A4), onset 1, length 1 beat; event 7: string 1 fret 7 (B4), onset 2, length 1 beat; event 8: string 1 fret 8 (C5), onset 3, length 0.5 beats; event 9: string 1 fret 7 (B4), onset 3&, length 0.5 beats; event 10: string 1 fret 5 (A4), onset 4, length 1 beat.

panels.label: Helper bar 3
panels.action: Helper only, bar 3: event 11: string 1 fret 3 (G4), onset 1, length 0.5 beats; event 12: string 1 fret 7 (B4), onset 1&, length 0.5 beats; event 13: string 1 fret 10 (D5), onset 2, length 1 beat; event 14: string 1 fret 8 (C5), onset 3, length 1 beat; event 15: string 1 fret 7 (B4), onset 4, length 1 beat.

panels.label: Helper bar 4
panels.action: Helper only, bar 4: event 16: string 1 fret 5 (A4), onset 1, length 1 beat; event 17: string 1 fret 8 (C5), onset 2, length 1 beat; event 18: string 1 fret 7 (B4), onset 3, length 0.5 beats; event 19: string 1 fret 5 (A4), onset 3&, length 0.5 beats; event 20: string 1 fret 3 (G4), onset 4, length 1 beat.

panels.label: Helper playback rule
panels.action: All four bars are in 4/4 and total sixteen beats. Give four count-in beats, then play the twenty events with the written durations and no extra ornament. Repeat the full phrase or one requested bar accurately; if the helper’s performance was uncertain, do not assign an accuracy percentage.

panels.label: Preserve the first answer
panels.action: Before revealing the helper key, write all four bars with note names and octaves or exact string/fret positions, plus each onset and duration in counted beats. Keep that first version; corrections belong on a second copy.

panels.label: Two scores
panels.action: The reference has twenty numbered events. Award one pitch point for the correct sounded note and octave at an event; award one rhythm point when both its onset and duration match. Keep pitch and rhythm totals separate, each out of twenty.

panels.label: Threshold and omissions
panels.action: The named 90% target needs at least 18/20 pitch points AND 18/20 rhythm points on the first full answer. Unexplained extra or missing events mean the form needs review rather than silently realigning events to inflate the totals.

panels.label: What invalidates the check
panels.action: Prior reading of the answer, copying visible notation, an inaccurate helper performance or unavailable source audio means this is practice without a valid fresh accuracy result. The app does not capture the answer or compute these percentages.

panels.label: Review
panels.action: After the first answer is kept, compare one missed interval or rhythm cell, hum or tap it, and play it accurately. A corrected copy demonstrates review, not a new unseen first attempt.

panels.label: Count and move
panels.action: In 4/4, say 1 e & a, 2 e & a, 3 e & a, 4 e & a. Keep down-up-down-up motion through each beat. Numbers and & are down motions; e and a are up motions.

panels.label: Exact contacts
panels.action: Contact the strings ONLY on 1, the a of 1, the & of 2, 3, the a of 3, and the & of 4. Directions: down, up, down, down, up, down. Every other motion passes clear of the strings.

panels.label: Hold across the missing beats
panels.action: Let each chord ring until the next written contact. In particular, the attacks on 1a and 3a sustain across the following numbered beats 2 and 4; do not insert a fresh attack there. A skipped attack here is not a full mute or rest.

panels.label: Start slowly
panels.action: Use a separate quarter-note metronome near 50–60 BPM. First practise the hand motion silently, then add the six contacts on one easy chord. Keep the a subdivisions evenly spaced rather than swinging them.

panels.label: Full bar and ending
panels.action: The six attack offsets from bar start are 0,0.75,1.5,2,2.75,3.5 beats. Sustain to the next attack or bar boundary. In a complete piece, keep this same cell for every bar and mute only at the final boundary.

l6-after-the-line-piece.name: After the Line — original twenty-four-bar piece

panels.label: One written cell throughout
panels.action: Use the sixteenth cell on every bar, with open Em,C,G,D diagrams. Each chord lasts two bars. Count four lead-in beats. At 100 BPM, the music is 24 four-beat bars with 144 written chord attacks.

panels.label: First section, bars 1–8
panels.action: Bar 1 Em; 2 Em; 3 C; 4 C; 5 G; 6 G; 7 D; 8 D. Apply the same six contacts and held-note pattern in each bar.

panels.label: Second section, bars 9–16
panels.action: Bar 9 Em; 10 Em; 11 C; 12 C; 13 G; 14 G; 15 D; 16 D. The form repeats, but the pulse must not accelerate.

panels.label: Final section, bars 17–24
panels.action: Bar 17 Em; 18 Em; 19 C; 20 C; 21 G; 22 G; 23 D; 24 D. Make the last contact on 24’s & of 4, sustain its final half beat, then mute at the following bar line.

panels.label: Practice versus target
panels.action: Start below 100 BPM and loop an exact transition as needed. For the named checkpoint, use actual 100 BPM and all 24 bars without a restart, omitted bar or added attack on beats 2/4. No performed audio or automatic pattern score is provided.

lessons.title: Barre Is Leverage, Not Strength
lessons.objective: Find a comfortable two-string mini barre and explain how partial F uses four sounding strings without clamping the whole neck.

steps.title: Support the instrument first
steps.action: Tune the open strings. Let your lap or strap support the guitar; take the fretting hand away briefly to check that the neck does not drop. Raise the neck a little if that makes the wrist easier to position.
steps.lookCheck: The shoulder is relaxed and the fretting hand can return without catching a falling neck. Use a clean, modest sound if amplified.
steps.listenCheck: Play an open string once, then mute it. A long effect tail would make the later release check harder to hear.

steps.title: Make the smallest barre
steps.action: Lay the index across strings 2 and 1 just behind fret 1, toward the guitar body within that fret space. Begin with gentle contact; add only enough pressure for each note to sound. Try a small roll toward the index finger’s thumb-facing edge if a soft crease sits on a string.
steps.lookCheck: One finger crosses two strings. It is beside the fret wire, not on top of it; the remaining fingers stay loose.
steps.listenCheck: Pick string 2, then string 1. Listen for two separate ringing notes, C then F. Stop and adjust one contact point if either is dead.

steps.title: Adjust support before pressure
steps.action: Place the thumb comfortably behind the neck, roughly opposite the index or middle finger. Move the elbow slightly until the index meets the two strings without a sharply bent wrist. Change one position at a time; avoid hauling the neck toward your body.
steps.lookCheck: The thumb is a light counter-support. There is no fixed elbow angle to force, and the guitar remains supported when pressure releases.
steps.listenCheck: Find the least pressure that still produces both notes. Extra pressure that does not improve the sound is not the objective.

steps.title: Build the four-string F
steps.action: Keep the short index barre. Put middle finger on string 3 fret 2 and ring finger on string 4 fret 3. Pick 4, 3, 2, 1, then make a small down-strum across those four strings only.
steps.lookCheck: The diagram is xx3211 from string 6 to 1. Curved middle and ring fingertips clear the next string; strings 6 and 5 are excluded.
steps.listenCheck: Hear F, A, C, F separately before the strum. The A is the major third; this partial shape is an F major chord, not an F5 power chord.

steps.title: Release deliberately
steps.action: Stop the strings with the picking hand, then remove the fretting fingers. Rest briefly and describe which placement adjustment improved the sound. Stop the attempt if there is pain or persistent discomfort.
steps.lookCheck: You can let go immediately; the grip does not remain clenched between attempts.
steps.listenCheck: The chord stops when intended, without an accidental open-string pull-off as the fretting hand leaves.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The B string rings but the high E is dead.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Check whether the index has lost contact with string 1. Move the small barre nearer fret 1 and change its angle slightly, then test only those two strings before rebuilding F.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The high E rings but the B string buzzes.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Look for a finger crease over string 2 or an index positioned too far from the fret wire. Reposition by a small amount; do not solve every buzz by squeezing harder.

mistakeRecovery.observation: Adding the middle finger kills a note that was clear.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Lift that finger and check the index pair again. Replace the middle fingertip on string 3, curving it enough to leave string 2 clear.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The thumb or wrist tightens while you hold the chord.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Mute and release. Recheck instrument support and try a shorter two-string attempt with a comfortable wrist; do not keep a painful shape held for the attention block.

practiceSegments.instruction: Tune, support the guitar, and test a relaxed fretting-hand approach.
Explore the two-string barre with short press, pick, and release attempts.
Adjust thumb, elbow and index placement one variable at a time.
Add the middle and ring fingers; check all four intended strings.
Rest, then explain the shape and one useful placement correction.

criteria: I can identify strings 4 through 1 as the sounding strings and 6 and 5 as excluded.
I can explain that the index spans B and high E at fret 1.
I found a brief, comfortable two-string barre and can release it immediately.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Explain the four-string shape and demonstrate a short, comfortable index barre. A first uneven full F is a reason to use the next placement exercise, not to hold more tension.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Return to the B/high-E pair, reposition near the fret wire, and release after each two-note check. Revisit support before adding more pressure.
selfAssessment.proves: A learner’s placement and comfort reflection, plus their own two-string listening check.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Automatic chord recognition, healthy-technique certification, four clean full entries, speed, or microphone-scored evidence.

lessons.title: Partial F, In and Out
lessons.objective: Build partial F from a released hand, diagnose each sounding string, and remove the shape without leaving tension behind.

steps.title: Read the entry sequence
steps.action: Use the four-string F diagram and the entry-check panels. Keep the metronome off: this exercise has no race or required change rate. Check standard tuning before working on the fretted notes.
steps.lookCheck: Read xx3211 from thick to thin string; two finger-1 dots mean one mini barre.
steps.listenCheck: If a fretted note seems far from the reference pitch, check tuning and fret choice before changing hand pressure.

steps.title: Start with two clear notes
steps.action: From fingers off, place the index across strings 2 and 1 at fret 1. Pick both once, release, and repeat at a comfortable pace. If only one rings, repair that contact before adding other fingers.
steps.lookCheck: The index lands beside fret 1 each time; the hand fully releases between tries.
steps.listenCheck: Both C4 and F4 should ring. Synthesized reference notes are pitch examples, not a recording of the desired guitar tone.

steps.title: Add and inspect the full shape
steps.action: Add middle on string 3 fret 2, ring on string 4 fret 3. Pick 4, 3, 2, 1 slowly. When a note fails, identify that string, lift the likely blocking finger, and rebuild just that part.
steps.lookCheck: Check fingertip clearance on adjacent strings; do not let the ring finger fall flat across string 3.
steps.listenCheck: Hear four distinct notes before judging the chord as a whole. One loud clear note must not hide a dead neighbour.

steps.title: Make one complete entry
steps.action: Start with fingers off, form F, inspect all four notes, make one small four-string down-strum, then mute and take the hand off. This entire cycle is one entry. Rest for a moment before the next.
steps.lookCheck: The picking motion begins at string 4. The hand resets rather than holding the same F for repeated strums.
steps.listenCheck: The strum contains the four intended notes and no low E or A. The release leaves no pitched string ringing.

steps.title: Repeat for recall, then choose a repair
steps.action: Try several new entries with the diagram, then one with the shape recalled before you look. Keep a mental or paper note of which string most often needs adjustment. Short rests are part of the practice.
steps.lookCheck: Do not change the shape or count a two-string version as a full F entry. Keep the same four-string target for comparison.
steps.listenCheck: Decide whether the issue is a muted neighbour, a buzz, an excluded bass string, or a noisy release; choose the matching correction.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The chord sounds acceptable as a strum but one string is dead.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Return to individual picking. Clear that string before counting a clean entry; a louder strum is not a repair.

mistakeRecovery.observation: A low bass string sneaks into the chord.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Shorten the downstroke and begin at string 4. Practise the picking path once with the fretting hand gently muting all strings, then rebuild F.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The chord is clean only while it stays held.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Practise fingers-off, place, inspect, release without any time target. Recall of the shape is the work; repeated strums of one held shape do not test it.

mistakeRecovery.observation: Open notes sound when the hand leaves.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Mute with the picking hand first. Lift the fretting fingers directly away without flicking a string sideways.

mistakeRecovery.observation: Each new attempt requires more squeezing.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Pause and let the hand relax. Recheck support and index contact, then do one two-string attempt before returning to all four.

practiceSegments.instruction: Read xx3211, check tuning, and leave the metronome off.
Make short two-string barre entries with a release between each.
Add the other fingers and diagnose individual-string failures.
Repeat full place, inspect, strum, mute, release cycles with short rests.
Recall the shape once, then name and practise the most useful repair.

criteria: I checked every intended string instead of judging only the loudest part of the strum.
I made more than one fresh full-shape entry, releasing my hand between them.
I can name the string or movement I need to improve next.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Make two fresh four-string entries that you judge clean and comfortable, then describe the repair you used. The following checkpoint separately asks for four consecutive entries.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Work on the weakest string in a short two- or three-finger fragment, then test a fresh full entry. Take as many short sessions as needed.
selfAssessment.proves: Self-reported placement practice and individual-string listening observations.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: An automatically counted trial, four consecutive successful entries, a changes-per-minute result, or measured chord quality.

lessons.title: Checkpoint: Four Clean Entries
lessons.objective: Demonstrate four consecutive fresh partial-F entries, with every intended string ringing and a complete release after each.

steps.title: Set an honest start
steps.action: Tune, read the four-entry protocol, and prepare a way to remember a count from zero to four. This is a self-counted accuracy check with no time limit; the five-minute plan is suggested practice time.
steps.lookCheck: Use the same xx3211 partial F for every entry. A diagram is allowed; declare to yourself whether you used it.
steps.listenCheck: Use a clean sound with no long delay or reverb so you can hear buzzes and the release.

steps.title: Inspect before counting
steps.action: From fingers off, build F. Pick strings 4, 3, 2, 1 separately, then down-strum just those four. All four notes must sound without a dead string or obvious buzz, and excluded bass strings must stay silent.
steps.lookCheck: The index covers 2 and 1; middle is on 3/2 and ring on 4/3. Check the fretted positions, not just the hand silhouette.
steps.listenCheck: Listen to F, A, C, F one at a time. A missing high F or muffled A makes this a repair attempt.

steps.title: Finish the entry and reset the hand
steps.action: Mute the strings with the picking hand, then take every fretting finger off. If the placement, four-note check, short strum and release all met the rule, advance your consecutive count by one.
steps.lookCheck: A held shape followed by four strums still counts as only one entry. Each next entry begins from a released hand.
steps.listenCheck: Listen after the release: there should be no accidental open-string note.

steps.title: Keep the consecutive rule
steps.action: Continue until you have four in a row. If any entry fails, stop, identify the failure, and reset the consecutive count to zero before a new series. Do not combine successful entries from separate broken series.
steps.lookCheck: Repair attempts are useful practice but do not become successful entries after several hidden adjustments. Rebuild from fingers off for the next counted entry.
steps.listenCheck: Name the failed string or noisy release before repeating; this keeps the check about sound rather than reaching a number.

steps.title: Report the actual result
steps.action: After the series, state your longest clean sequence and one observation. If four happened, repeat this checkpoint on a later day to check retention. If it did not, return to the placement exercise with the actual weak string.
steps.lookCheck: Do not treat finishing the attention blocks or opening the lesson as a four-entry result. No automatic counter is provided for this F exercise.
steps.listenCheck: A clean result means your own listening found all four intended notes and controlled releases in that series.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The third entry fails after two clear ones.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Keep the two as practice history in your own notes, but restart the consecutive count at zero after the repair.

mistakeRecovery.observation: I fixed a string while holding the shape and counted the repaired chord.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Use that adjustment to learn the placement. Release completely and test a new entry before advancing the count.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The bass strings ring although the fretted notes are clear.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Practise the four-string picking path and the picking-hand stop. The next counted series must include quiet excluded strings.

mistakeRecovery.observation: I am rushing to fit four entries inside the lesson time.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Pause the check. There is no speed requirement or deadline; rest and rebuild at a pace that lets you hear each string.

practiceSegments.instruction: Tune and read the complete-entry and consecutive-count rules.
Make warm-up entries; choose one placement repair before the check.
Attempt a fresh four-entry series, inspecting and releasing each shape.
Rest, repair any failed string, then attempt a new complete series if comfortable.
State the actual longest sequence and the next review action.

criteria: I started each counted entry with all fretting fingers off.
In each of four consecutive entries I heard all four intended notes and kept strings 6 and 5 quiet.
Each entry ended with a controlled mute and released hand.
A failed entry reset my consecutive count; I did not add separate partial series.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Your own check reaches four consecutive fresh entries that meet every criterion, without discomfort. This fulfills the named self-assessed accuracy target for this shape.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Record the actual longest sequence, repair the specific string or release, and return to Partial F, In and Out. A partial series remains practice, not a completed four-entry check.
selfAssessment.proves: A learner-reported series of four independent partial-F placements and releases.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Microphone verification, a timed change count, full six-string barre proficiency, technique certification, or long-term retention.

lessons.title: Two Notes, No Quality
lessons.objective: Identify a power chord’s root and fifth, add an octave without adding a third, and move the shape while controlling unused strings.

steps.title: Hear the two-note G5
steps.action: Use standard tuning. Put index on string 6 fret 3 and ring on string 5 fret 5. Pick the two strings separately, then together with a small downstroke. Keep the other four strings silent.
steps.lookCheck: The root is the lower G on string 6. The D on string 5 is its perfect fifth: seven semitones above this G.
steps.listenCheck: Hear G then D. Neither a B nor a B-flat is included, so this voicing does not supply the third that distinguishes G major from G minor.

steps.title: Add the repeated root
steps.action: Add little finger on string 4 fret 5 while retaining the two-note shape. Compare the two-string version with the three-string version at the same gentle volume.
steps.lookCheck: The added note is another G, one octave above the root. Three sounding strings do not necessarily mean three different note names.
steps.listenCheck: The extra string thickens the voicing without supplying a major or minor third. The 5 in G5 names the fifth, not the number of fingers.

steps.title: Move the root, keep the spacing
steps.action: Move the complete three-string G5 shape up two frets to A5: 5, 7, 7 on strings 6, 5, 4. Release fretting pressure during the move while keeping gentle string contact, then settle before picking.
steps.lookCheck: The ring and little fingers remain two frets above the index. Follow the index root to fret 5 rather than moving each finger independently at random.
steps.listenCheck: Hear A, E, A. There should be no unintended open-string note between G5 and A5.

steps.title: Move to a fifth-string root
steps.action: Build C5 with index on string 5 fret 3, ring on string 4 fret 5, little finger on string 3 fret 5. Begin the pick stroke on string 5; let a light touch of the index tip silence string 6 without fretting it.
steps.lookCheck: Use the C5 diagram: x355xx. The root string changed, so the previous six-string-root picking path must change too.
steps.listenCheck: Hear C, G, C. A ringing low E adds an unwanted note for this exercise; listen to that string separately while gently brushing it to test the mute.

steps.title: Separate muting from silence between chords
steps.action: Let unused higher strings touch the relaxed underside of a fretting finger while the intended fingertips stay clear. Strum the intended group, then stop all vibration using picking-hand contact and released fretting pressure. Rebuild before the next strum.
steps.lookCheck: Muted strings are touched lightly, not pressed into extra notes. Palm-muted tone while playing and a complete stop between attacks are different actions.
steps.listenCheck: An intentional light brush of an excluded string should make no clear pitch. After the stop, listen for silence rather than a sustained muted chord.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The little finger mutes the fifth instead of adding the octave.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Lift it, confirm the two-note version, then replace it with the fingertip on the octave string. Keep the ring fingertip clear of that neighbouring string.

mistakeRecovery.observation: C5 sounds larger than expected.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Check that the downstroke starts on string 5 and that string 6 is lightly muted. Do not use the open low E as part of this C5 voicing.

mistakeRecovery.observation: Moving G5 to A5 produces a loud slide or an open note.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Reduce pressure while retaining light contact, keep the picking hand still, and move during a silent beat. Plant the new frets before sounding them.

mistakeRecovery.observation: I call the three-string shape major because it has three notes.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Name the pitches aloud: G, D, G. The repeated G is an octave, and there is still no B or B-flat third.

mistakeRecovery.observation: Every string goes dead when I try to mute.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: First restore the clear two-note root and fifth. Add contact only to an unused string at a time; keep the active fingertips curved enough to avoid their neighbours.

practiceSegments.instruction: Build and compare the separate notes of two-string G5.
Add the octave and explain why it is still G5.
Move G5 to A5 slowly, with a silent transition.
Build fifth-string-root C5 and test its excluded strings.
Alternate a clear chord with a complete stop; recap root, fifth and octave.

criteria: I can name the root and fifth in G5, A5 and C5.
I can explain why adding the root’s octave does not add a major or minor third.
I can play the two- and three-string G5 versions and identify the correct starting string for C5.
I can stop a chord and test that an unused string is muted.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Explain the missing-third idea and demonstrate both G5 voicings plus a deliberate, quiet move to A5 or C5. Use the next lesson for repeated changes in time.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Return to two-string G5, then add one task at a time: octave, slide, fifth-string root, and excluded-string muting.
selfAssessment.proves: A learner’s interval explanation and self-checked shape and muting practice.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Automatic recognition of simultaneous notes, measured muting, a 110-BPM result, or a rule that every song can use power chords in place of its written harmony.

lessons.title: Power-Chord Riff Song
lessons.objective: Play Switchyard, an original sixteen-bar G5–A5–C5 piece, with two attacks and two deliberate rests per bar.

steps.title: Read the whole piece
steps.action: Use the Switchyard bar map. It has A, B, returning A, and ending sections, four bars each. Use the three-string G5, A5 and C5 voicings; standard tuning, no capo. Read all sixteen chord names before playing.
steps.lookCheck: Each chord label fills one bar. Bars 9–12 repeat bars 1–4; the ending at 13–16 is C5, A5, G5, G5.
steps.listenCheck: Sound each shape separately at a clean, modest volume. Stop the synthesized pitch references before starting the metronome.

steps.title: Learn the riff cell on one chord
steps.action: Keep the map visible and use a separate metronome at 60 BPM with quarter-note clicks in 4/4, or a slower setting you can control. If using the iOS Practice metronome, copy the bar map before opening it. On G5: downstroke on 1, stop on 2, downstroke on 3, stop on 4. Repeat while counting every beat.
steps.lookCheck: Make two downstrokes per bar. Beats 2 and 4 are full rests, not extra muted strums. Let the picking hand return above the strings without striking them.
steps.listenCheck: The sound starts with beats 1 and 3 and ends at beats 2 and 4. A muted but still pitched sustain is not the complete rest this riff asks for.

steps.title: Prepare changes during the rest
steps.action: Practise one G5 bar into one A5 bar, then one G5 bar into one C5 bar. On silent beat 4, keep the strings muted and aim the next root; land the entire shape for the next beat 1.
steps.lookCheck: A5 uses frets 5,7,7 on strings 6,5,4. C5 uses frets 3,5,5 on 5,4,3, so move the picking start to string 5.
steps.listenCheck: No open string should sound in the move. If the new chord is late, lower the working tempo rather than shortening the preceding bar.

steps.title: Join four-bar sections
steps.action: Give yourself four count-in clicks and play bars 1–4. Repeat that section until the cell and chord order are clear, then practise 5–8 and 13–16. Count through a missed attack and re-enter at the next section during rehearsal.
steps.lookCheck: The map remains visible. Do not jump from a missed chord into the next bar early to catch up.
steps.listenCheck: Keep the click and rests audible. Notice whether C5 introduces a low E, or an upward move leaves a ringing slide.

steps.title: Play the full form
steps.action: After four count-in beats, play bars 1 through 16 without stopping the click. Every bar uses the same cell, including bar 16; mute on its beat 4 and finish. The complete piece contains 32 attacks and no extra ending strum.
steps.lookCheck: Follow A, B, A, ending. If you restart or skip a bar, remember where it happened and describe the take as interrupted.
steps.listenCheck: The last rest should be as controlled as the first. Listen for the same pulse when A returns, rather than accelerating because it is familiar.

steps.title: Choose the next practice tempo
steps.action: State the tempo you actually used, whether every bar was played, and one specific bar to repair. If the full form was clear, raise the available metronome setting a small amount and repeat a short section first. The later checkpoint target is 110 BPM.
steps.lookCheck: This is a written piece played to a separate metronome. There is no automatic bar-following backing track or polyphonic score for it.
steps.listenCheck: Judge timing and muting separately. Reaching the last bar does not prove every chord was clean.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The pick strums on all four clicks.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Stay on G5 and say play, stop, play, stop for four bars. Use the picking hand to silence on 2 and 4, without another downstroke.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The move to C5 includes the low E.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Loop G5 into C5 slowly. Aim the next root on string 5 during beat 4 and check the low-E mute before the next attack.

mistakeRecovery.observation: I lose my place at the returning A section.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Read bars 9–12 aloud, then practise bars 7–10 so the transition into the repeat is familiar. Keep counting four beats per bar.

mistakeRecovery.observation: I speed up as soon as the shape repeats.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Keep the same quarter-note click running through two consecutive G5 bars. Count the silent beats aloud; do not use chord changes as the only timing landmarks.

mistakeRecovery.observation: I miss a chord and restart the whole piece immediately.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: During rehearsal, mute and keep counting to the next four-bar section, then re-enter. After the take, loop the failed change. Call the recovered take interrupted rather than a continuous full performance.

practiceSegments.instruction: Read all sixteen bars and check the three chord shapes.
Practise the play, stop, play, stop cell on G5 with quarter-note clicks.
Loop G5–A5 and G5–C5 changes at a controllable tempo.
Practise the four-bar sections, including the ending.
Count in and play the complete sixteen-bar form at the chosen tempo.
State actual tempo, continuity, mute quality, and one repair bar.

criteria: I can follow all sixteen bars and identify the A, B, A and ending sections.
I use downstrokes on 1 and 3, with full rests on 2 and 4.
I know when the root moves from string 6 to string 5.
I can state my actual tempo and whether the full take included a restart, skipped bar or recovery.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Play the whole sixteen-bar piece at a controllable tempo with its written attacks and rests, and identify any remaining repair. The 110-BPM checkpoint is a separate next step.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Loop the exact transition that failed at a slower available tempo, then connect it to the bar before and after. Keep interrupted attempts distinct from full takes.
selfAssessment.proves: Self-reported practice of a complete original piece at the learner’s stated tempo.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Automatic play-along completion, measured chord correctness or muting, a 110-BPM checkpoint, or performance of a licensed commercial song.

lessons.title: Checkpoint: Riff at One Hundred and Ten
lessons.sourceTitle: Checkpoint: Riff at One Hundred and Ten
lessons.objective: Play all sixteen bars of Switchyard at 110 BPM with the written chord changes, on-beat attacks, and fully muted rests, then report the result honestly.

steps.title: Check the target and the sound
steps.action: Use the same three-string G5, A5 and C5 voicings and sixteen-bar map as the song lesson. Tune and check each chord’s individual strings. Keep the map visible and set a separate metronome to exactly 110 BPM, quarter-note clicks, 4/4. If using the iOS Practice metronome, copy the map before opening it.
steps.lookCheck: The tempo is 110, not a percentage label or an estimated speed. Keep the bar map available; memorization is not part of this checkpoint.
steps.listenCheck: Use a clean sound so unwanted open strings and incomplete stops remain audible. A click is timing support, not a recording of your performance.

steps.title: Confirm the pulse before the full take
steps.action: At 110, play the G5 riff cell for two bars: sound on 1 and 3, silence on 2 and 4. If the cell already feels uncontrolled, return to a slower practice tempo before attempting the complete checkpoint.
steps.lookCheck: There are two attacks per four-beat bar. Do not convert the clicks to eighth notes or omit the silent beats to make the number easier.
steps.listenCheck: The two starts align with the intended clicks; no pitched note carries through the full-rest beats.

steps.title: Count in and play all sixteen bars
steps.action: Count four silent clicks, then begin bar 1. Follow A at 1–4, B at 5–8, A at 9–12, and ending at 13–16. Make both attacks in the final bar and stop on beat 4.
steps.lookCheck: Use the silent beat 4 to prepare each change without an extra strum. C5 starts on string 5; G5 and A5 start on string 6.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for 32 intended attacks, quiet transitions, and full stops on 2 and 4. Do not let a clean root hide a dead fifth or octave.

steps.title: Separate a full take from a recovered take
steps.action: If you miss a bar or stop, keep the attempt as practice and name its interruption. Repair that section after resting, then use a new four-beat count-in for another complete take. Do not splice two partial runs into one result.
steps.lookCheck: The checkpoint form is 16 bars without restarts or skipped bars. Recovering later is useful practice, but it does not erase an earlier interruption.
steps.listenCheck: Check whether the rests stayed quiet through the fastest-feeling change, especially C5 to A5 in bars 13–14.

steps.title: Review the named goal
steps.action: State the actual tempo, whether every bar and attack was played, and whether any buzz, wrong string or pitched rest remained. Claim the 110-BPM target only when this full take meets every criterion. Otherwise state the working tempo and exact repair bar.
steps.lookCheck: A completed lesson screen or elapsed metronome time is not proof of the performance. These judgments are yours; this checkpoint has no chord-recognition score.
steps.listenCheck: Judge the sound you actually heard. If unsure about one section, treat it as needing review and repeat that section before the next full take.

mistakeRecovery.observation: 110 BPM is selected but I am playing once every two clicks.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Count all four beats and use the specified two attacks per bar. Verify the cell on one chord before counting a full take.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The chord is correct but its sound runs across beat 2 or 4.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Practise a firm, quiet picking-hand stop on those beats at a slower tempo, then restore 110. Palm-muted sustain still contains pitch and is not a full rest.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The complete map fits only if I shorten a bar at a change.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Repeat that two-bar transition slowly while counting four beats in each bar. Restore the target tempo only after the full-length bars remain intact.

mistakeRecovery.observation: I play the first half cleanly and restart the second half.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Keep both sections as rehearsal. For this checkpoint, begin a fresh full take with a count-in and preserve the complete order without splicing.

mistakeRecovery.observation: I finish at 100 BPM and want to count the 110-BPM goal.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Keep the successful 100-BPM take as progress and practise a short section at the next comfortable setting. The named target remains 110 BPM; do not relabel a slower take.

practiceSegments.instruction: Tune, inspect the three voicings, and read the full-take criteria.
Set 110 BPM and check the cell on G5; return to practice if uncontrolled.
Take four count-in beats and play the complete sixteen-bar map.
Rest and repair one exact transition; make a fresh full take only if ready.
Review actual tempo, all-bar continuity, intended strings and quiet rests.

criteria: The metronome was set to 110 BPM with a quarter-note click in 4/4.
After four count-in beats, I played all 16 bars in order without restarting or skipping a bar.
I made the 32 written attacks on beats 1 and 3 with the intended three-string voicings.
I stopped the sound on every beat 2 and 4, including the final stop, with no unwanted pitched string ringing.
I can distinguish this full take from earlier slower, interrupted or repaired practice.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: A full self-reviewed sixteen-bar take at 110 BPM meets every listed condition. Recheck another day before treating the skill as retained.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Keep the actual working tempo and the first failed bar in your practice notes. Repair its transition or mute at a slower setting, then make a new full 110-BPM take when ready.
selfAssessment.proves: A learner-reported full performance of this specific original riff at the stated 110-BPM target.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Microphone-certified pitch, rhythm, chord voicing or muting; automated bar counting; mastery of other power-chord riffs; or long-term retention.

lessons.title: The Form You Already Know
lessons.objective: Locate the three four-bar lines of one standard A blues form and connect A7, D7 and E7 to I7, IV7 and V7.

steps.title: Choose one form
steps.action: Read the twelve-bar panel map. This version keeps A7 for bars 1–4; it does not use a quick change in bar 2. One chorus means one complete trip through all twelve bars.
steps.lookCheck: Point to bar 5, then bar 9: these are the starts of the second and third lines.
steps.listenCheck: Say twelve groups of four beats; the chord staying the same does not stop the bar count.

steps.title: Check the three chord colours
steps.action: Use the A7, D7 and E7 diagrams. Pick their intended strings separately, then strum each gently. These dominant-seventh chords add a seventh to the major-chord sound you know.
steps.lookCheck: A7 starts on string 5, D7 on string 4, E7 on string 6. Follow the X markers instead of sweeping all six automatically.
steps.listenCheck: Hear the open strings clearly, especially G in A7 and D in E7. These notes are part of the intended seventh chords.

steps.title: Play the counted skeleton
steps.action: Use a separate metronome at about 60 BPM. After four count-in beats, strum once on beat 1 of every bar and let it ring through the remaining beats. Say the bar number on beat 1.
steps.lookCheck: Keep the map visible. If using iOS Practice > Metronome, copy the map before opening that sheet.
steps.listenCheck: Hear four even beats in every bar, with a clear change at bars 5, 7, 9, 10, 11 and 12.

steps.title: Hear the return
steps.action: Play bars 9–12, then bar 1 of the next chorus without adding a gap. E7 at the end points back toward A7. Stop afterward and recite the three lines.
steps.lookCheck: A new chorus starts directly after bar 12; there is no new count-in between choruses.
steps.listenCheck: Listen to E7 returning to A7, then distinguish that return from a restart caused by losing place.

mistakeRecovery.observation: I treat four A7 bars as one long bar.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Say 1-2-3-4, 2-2-3-4, 3-2-3-4, 4-2-3-4 before D7. Keep separate bar numbers.

mistakeRecovery.observation: I switch to D7 in bar 2.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: That is a different valid blues variant, but this exercise uses A7 throughout bars 1–4. Re-read the selected map.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The return adds an extra bar of E7.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Loop bars 11, 12 and next 1; count four beats in each and change directly to A7.

practiceSegments.instruction: Read the three four-bar lines and identify the home chord.
Check A7, D7 and E7 one string at a time.
Play the twelve-bar skeleton with one stroke per bar.
Connect the last line back to the first and recite the form.

criteria: I can point to the starts of the three lines.
I connect A7, D7 and E7 to I7, IV7 and V7.
I understand a chorus has twelve four-beat bars in this version.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Explain the selected form and follow one counted chorus with the map.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Practise the last four bars and the return to A7, then rebuild the full map.
selfAssessment.proves: Self-checked understanding of one twelve-bar variant and its three chords.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Memory recall, shuffle feel, three uninterrupted choruses or automatic chord recognition.

lessons.title: Call the Changes
lessons.objective: Prepare the next chord one bar ahead, then reduce spoken prompts while retaining the twelve-bar order.

steps.title: Prepare your own calls
steps.action: Read the call guide and twelve-bar map. Speak the NEXT bar’s chord on beat 4 of the current bar. You or a practice partner provide the calls; this lesson does not generate an automatic spoken cue.
steps.lookCheck: Distinguish a chord name from a bar number: say A-seven, D-seven or E-seven.
steps.listenCheck: Say a call while keeping four evenly spaced beats; do not speed through the final beat.

steps.title: Call without the guitar first
steps.action: At a comfortable click, count one chorus and speak every next-bar chord. In bar 4 call D7; in bar 8 call E7; in bar 12 call A7 for the next chorus.
steps.lookCheck: Your eyes may follow the map during this first pass. You are reading ahead, not changing early.
steps.listenCheck: The call on beat 4 anticipates the next downbeat while the current bar still lasts four beats.

steps.title: Add one strum per bar
steps.action: Play the current chord on beat 1, then call the next chord on beat 4. Loop bars 8–12 into 1 if the final line overloads your attention.
steps.lookCheck: Do not move to the called chord until the next beat 1. Prepare the fingers silently during the last beat.
steps.listenCheck: The chord sound changes at the bar line, not at the spoken cue.

steps.title: Fade the prompts
steps.action: On the next chorus, call only before a real chord change. Then cover the guide and try a chorus with calls from memory; finally keep only the bar count.
steps.lookCheck: Cover both the map and the call guide, or turn away. There is no automatic cue-fading switch.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for even time as the speech gets quieter; losing the spoken cue must not remove a beat.

steps.title: Locate the first uncertainty
steps.action: State the first bar where you needed the chart. Practise that bar plus the bar before and after, then rejoin a full chorus.
steps.lookCheck: A glance at the chart means supported practice, not chart-free recall.
steps.listenCheck: Keep the chord-quality check separate from remembering the order.

mistakeRecovery.observation: I play the next chord as soon as I say it.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Keep the picking hand still on beat 4. Place the next chord only for the following beat 1.

mistakeRecovery.observation: Speaking and playing break the pulse.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Return to spoken calls only, then add one downstroke per bar. Use a slower click.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The last four calls become scrambled.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Speak E7, D7, A7, E7 over bars 9–12 first; then rehearse the one-bar-ahead call sequence from bar 8.

practiceSegments.instruction: Read the manual cue rule and mark the six change points.
Speak one-bar-ahead cues without playing.
Add a current-chord strum on each first beat.
Reduce cues, cover the guide, and try memory-led choruses.
Repair the first uncertain transition and state what support remained.

criteria: My spoken cue comes before the change while the chord changes on the next downbeat.
I can call the final line and its return to A7.
I distinguish chart-supported, spoken and silent practice.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Play a full chorus with correctly anticipated changes, then identify whether you still need spoken or visual prompts.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Repeat a three-bar window around the first uncertain change and reduce only one kind of support at a time.
selfAssessment.proves: Self-reported anticipatory cue practice and form navigation.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Automated chord calls, speech detection, chart-free three-chorus recall or measured timing.

lessons.title: Checkpoint: Three Choruses From Memory
lessons.objective: Play three consecutive twelve-bar choruses in the chosen A blues form without looking at a chart.

steps.title: Set the memory rule
steps.action: Review the form once, choose a comfortable quarter-note tempo, then cover the form, call guide and chord diagrams or turn the screen away. You may count bars aloud, but do not read chord names or accept spoken chord prompts.
steps.lookCheck: The goal is three complete choruses, 36 bars. There is no required catalog tempo; record the one you use.
steps.listenCheck: Check the click before starting; it supplies pulse but no chord answers.

steps.title: Count in once
steps.action: Take four count-in beats and play one downstroke per bar. Hold the exact form used in the teaching lesson, including A7 throughout bars 1–4 and E7 in bar 12.
steps.lookCheck: Keep the same chord version throughout. Changing to another blues variant midway is not this recall check.
steps.listenCheck: Each bar contains four beats even when the chord repeats.

steps.title: Connect all three choruses
steps.action: Go straight from bar 12 to the next bar 1. Repeat twice more, counting chorus 1, 2 and 3 as you begin them. Mute after the final beat of chorus 3; do not add an extra ending bar.
steps.lookCheck: No chart glance, extra count-in, stopped click or skipped bar inside the 36-bar take.
steps.listenCheck: Listen for smooth returns from E7 to A7 and an unchanged pulse at each new chorus.

steps.title: Review without rewriting the take
steps.action: Uncover the map after stopping and compare the sequence you played. State whether any memory hesitation, wrong change, added bar or external cue occurred.
steps.lookCheck: A repaired take is practice. Start a new full attempt if the chart was needed; do not combine shorter successful sections.
steps.listenCheck: Note chord clarity separately: knowing the order does not automatically make every string clean.

mistakeRecovery.observation: I lose the chorus number.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: During rehearsal, say first, second or third on each return to bar 1. Keep that neutral count in the memory check.

mistakeRecovery.observation: I glance at the chart to rescue bar 9.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Label the run supported practice. Loop bars 8–10 with the chart, then begin a fresh chart-free three-chorus take.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The last chord of a chorus gets five beats.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Practise bar 12 into 1 with four beats per bar, then reconnect the complete form.

practiceSegments.instruction: Review the map and choose the actual tempo.
Rehearse the two chorus boundaries, then cover all chord prompts.
Attempt one uninterrupted 36-bar memory take with one initial count-in.
Compare the recalled sequence with the map and locate any error.
State the result and the next repair or retention check.

criteria: I played the same twelve-bar version three times in order.
I used no chart or chord-name prompts during the take.
All 36 bars kept four beats, with no extra gap between choruses.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Self-review confirms three consecutive complete choruses from memory; recheck on another day for retention.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Keep the actual first error and practise its three-bar neighbourhood. A supported or partial take does not meet the memory target.
selfAssessment.proves: Learner-reported recall and continuity across this specific 36-bar form.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Automatic chart hiding, verified recall percentage, certified chord quality, other blues variants or long-term retention.

lessons.title: Four Bars Is a Sentence
lessons.objective: Shape a four-bar blues phrase with a clear opening, an answer and intentional space while the underlying pulse continues.

steps.title: Choose the note language
steps.action: Use the A minor-pentatonic map: A, C, D, E, G. Begin with A at string 1 fret 5 and C at fret 8; add E at fret 12 only when moving there comfortably.
steps.lookCheck: Move the hand between positions rather than stretching across seven frets. The palette is A blues vocabulary, not the A-major scale.
steps.listenCheck: C adds a blues colour against the C# inside A7. Return to A to hear home; do not assume every sustained note blends equally with every chord.

steps.title: Make a short question
steps.action: Count one bar of four beats. Play A on 1, C on 2, then either hold C or leave space through 3 and 4. Repeat the same small idea so you can recognize it.
steps.lookCheck: Two intentional notes are enough. You do not need to run the whole scale.
steps.listenCheck: Hear a recognizable rhythm, followed by an ending or breath.

steps.title: Answer and leave space
steps.action: Over the next bar, answer with C then A, using a different rhythm. Let bar 3 rest while you keep counting; use bar 4 for one final A.
steps.lookCheck: A full bar of planned silence still occupies four beats. A restart after losing count does not.
steps.listenCheck: The answer feels connected because it shares notes or rhythm; the final A settles the phrase.

steps.title: Place it in the blues form
steps.action: Use a partner or your own separately recorded accompaniment playing the taught twelve-bar A blues. Enter on bar 1 and improvise through bars 1–4, which are A7 in this version. Without accompaniment, rehearse with a click and label it solo preparation.
steps.lookCheck: Confirm the start of the chorus with your partner or recording; no backing track is supplied in this lesson.
steps.listenCheck: Keep hearing the four-bar boundary under your pauses. Stop your phrase in time for the change to D7 at bar 5.

mistakeRecovery.observation: I fill every beat because silence feels like stopping.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Plan one full rest bar and count it aloud. Continue the pulse, then land on the next intended beat.

mistakeRecovery.observation: My fingers keep moving while I cannot hear an idea.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Limit the phrase to A and C. Repeat one rhythm before adding another note.

mistakeRecovery.observation: I use the wrong backing key or do not know the entry bar.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Confirm A blues and bar 1 before playing. A click-only phrase is preparation, not evidence of following the blues form.

practiceSegments.instruction: Find A and C, then inspect the rest of the note palette.
Create and repeat a one-bar question.
Answer it, count a rest bar and make a final landing.
Place the four-bar idea over known A-blues accompaniment, if available.
Describe the phrase boundary and whether accompaniment was used.

criteria: I can recognize my opening idea and its answer.
I count through intentional rests.
I know the phrase occupies bars 1–4 of the selected blues form.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Demonstrate a counted four-bar phrase with a related answer and planned space; identify whether it was played with accompaniment.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Use two notes and a click until the four-bar shape holds; add known accompaniment afterward.
selfAssessment.proves: Self-reviewed phrase structure and pulse awareness.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Automatic improvisation grading, backing-track playback, scale recognition or over-form performance when rehearsed with a click alone.

lessons.title: One Phrase, Three Answers
lessons.objective: Use an original one-bar question to invent three related answers with different rhythms, endings or rests.

steps.title: Learn the supplied question
steps.action: Read the A–C–E seed: string 1 frets 5, 8, 12 on beats 1, 2, 3, with E held through 4. Tap individual reference cells if useful, then play or sing the rhythm yourself.
steps.lookCheck: The buttons sound one pitch at a time; there is no automatic complete-phrase performance. Shift the hand for fret 12.
steps.listenCheck: Hear the upward question and its two-beat last note.

steps.title: Hear three kinds of response
steps.action: Read the three written answer examples. First change the ending to A; then retain the seed rhythm with a different note order; then begin with a rest. Play them slowly without treating them as required improvisations.
steps.lookCheck: Each answer occupies exactly one four-beat bar. A note on beat 3 may hold through beat 4.
steps.listenCheck: The examples remain related even though the rhythm or ending changes.

steps.title: Invent your own first answer
steps.action: Repeat the original question, then invent a one-bar response using A, C or E. Choose one deliberate difference, such as a longer A at the end.
steps.lookCheck: Do not copy the supplied answer and label it newly improvised. Keep the bar count audible.
steps.listenCheck: Decide whether the response sounds like an answer rather than another unrelated scale run.

steps.title: Make two more answers
steps.action: Return to the same question before each new response. Change a different feature for each: rhythm, final note or placement of a rest. Stay inside A, C, D, E, G if adding notes.
steps.lookCheck: Use three separate question-answer pairs during rehearsal; these are not three stitched attempts at the later continuity checkpoint.
steps.listenCheck: Identify the audible difference between your three answers.

steps.title: Join a four-bar exchange
steps.action: Play the question in bar 1 and your three answers in bars 2–4 with a continuous pulse. Use known A-blues accompaniment if available; otherwise label this click-only phrase practice.
steps.lookCheck: No supplied backing or recorded prompt is implied. A planned rest preserves the count; a restart changes the take.
steps.listenCheck: Leave the final note in a place that lets you hear bar 5 coming.

mistakeRecovery.observation: All three answers are the same notes at the same times.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Keep the notes for one answer but move its first attack to beat 2. For another, change only its ending.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The question itself keeps changing.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Repeat the written seed until you can recall it, then hold that question constant while varying answers.

mistakeRecovery.observation: Moving to fret 12 breaks the count.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Practise the shift slowly, or rehearse answers on A and C while separately learning the seed. Do not stretch the hand across the full distance.

practiceSegments.instruction: Hear the separate seed pitches and play its written rhythm.
Explore the three supplied answer types.
Invent and repeat your first two distinct responses.
Invent a third response and join the four-bar exchange.
Name the differences and review pulse, palette and accompaniment use.

criteria: I can play the same one-bar seed before each response.
My three answers differ in an audible, describable way.
I keep each response inside its allotted bar and intended note palette.
selfAssessment.readyWhen: Demonstrate three distinct self-authored responses to the same seed, then connect the question and answers in a four-bar rehearsal.
selfAssessment.ifNotReady: Change one feature at a time and keep the seed fixed. Rehearse the fret shift separately if it overwhelms phrasing.
selfAssessment.proves: Self-reported phrase variation and counted call-and-answer practice.
selfAssessment.doesNotProve: Automatic phrase playback, originality detection, measured timing or a completed over-blues checkpoint without accompaniment.

lessons.title: Checkpoint: Four Bars, In Key, No Stop
lessons.sourceTitle: Checkpoint: Four Bars, In Key, No Stop
lessons.objective: Improvise one complete four-bar phrase from the A-blues note palette while staying with bars 1–4 of known twelve-bar accompaniment.

steps.title: Set a real accompaniment context
steps.action: Use a partner or your own separate recording playing the exact A7/D7/E7 twelve-bar map. Confirm the tempo and chorus start. There is no supplied backing track here; a click alone supports rehearsal but cannot establish the over-form part of this target.
